curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42116-1-1.pdf (one book; the functions page is page 64; the set's B model isn't in it)

functions.does: The black 12 tooth gear on top of the cage, at its back, raises and lowers the loader arm: its upright shaft turns a 20 tooth gear whose shaft carries a worm, the worm turns a 20 tooth gear on a cross shaft at the back, and a crank on that shaft pushes the arm's lower white beam up through a short link.
functions.source: book: steps 11-17 (the upright shaft, worm and gears), page 28 (the inset with arrows: the upright shaft turning, the red crank rising and falling), steps 29-30 (the cross shaft, its crank and the arm), page 64 (the knob on top, and the arm raised)

functions.does: The black 12 tooth gear on the right side at the back tilts the bucket: its shaft carries a crank at the arm's pivot, which slides the arm's upper white beam along the lower one, and the upper beam tips the bucket at the front.
functions.source: book: steps 30-34 (the two white beams and the links between them), step 41 (the gear on the yellow axle), page 64 (the gear turned, the bucket tipping)

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely; there's no steering and no drive to them.
The worm holds the arm where it's left, so the arm doesn't drop under the bucket's weight.
functions.source: inferred: a worm drive can't be turned back from the arm
functions.skip: only matters under gravity; the knob works the arm both ways without it
